body.statement:
Let \(h_s\) be selected by the normalized-shape rule in \texttt{def:feasible-estimator}.  For a sufficiently large fixed initial-scale constant and some fixed \(A>2\lambda/d+2\), uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)\), every cohort and every integer \(v\ge0\) with \(2^vh_{s,\beta}\le1\) satisfy
\[
P\{h_s>2^vh_{s,\beta}\mid E_0,\widetilde z_s\}
\le C\exp(-c2^{vd})+CT^{-A}.
\]
Consequently, for every fixed \(a>0\),
\[
\mathbb E_P[h_s^a\mathbf1_{\mathrm{good}}\mid E_0,\widetilde z_s]
\le C\left\{(Tn_s)^{-a/(2\lambda+d)}
+\left(\frac{\log(T\vee2)}T\right)^{a/d}
+N^{-a/2}\right\}.
\]
The terminal-grid failure probability is at most \(C\exp\{-cT/\log(T\vee2)\}+CT^{-A}\), and the total bad-sample probability in \texttt{def:honest-interval} is at most \(CR_{\star,\beta}\) along the stated arrays.  These bounds remain valid when the uninflated smoothing-scale local count \(T\{(Tn_s)^{-1/(2\lambda+d)}\}^d\) is \(O(1)\); the selected log-adjusted initial scale itself satisfies \(Th_{s,\beta}^d\ge c\log(T\vee2)\).  No exogenous dense-local-site or upper-local-mass condition is imposed.
body.justification: Alternating calendar-block coupling and bounded matrix concentration give the log-adjusted bandwidth moment using only design mixing.

body.consumer: The estimator and interval attain their rates in every relative-growth regime.
body.proof_tex:
Condition throughout on \((E_0,\widetilde z_s=z)\).  By \texttt{ass:donor-independence}, this extra conditioning does not change the conditional law of the historical design.  By the revised \texttt{ass:temporal-mixing}, that design process alone obeys the declared geometric absolute-regularity bound; no condition on the outcome path is used below.  For \(z\in[0,1]^d\) and \(0<h\le1\), define
\[
\ell_{z,h}(x)=K((x-z)/h),
\qquad
\Phi_{z,h}(x)=K((x-z)/h)b_r((x-z)/h)b_r((x-z)/h)^\top.
\]
Bounded support of \(K\), the density bounds, and the change of variables \(x=z+hu\) give a constant \(C_0<\infty\) such that
\[
\mathbb E_P[\ell_{z,h}(X_{st})\mid E_0]\le C_0h^d.
\tag{14}
\]
There is also a uniform lower bound.  Choose \(\eta>0\) and \(k_0>0\) such that \(K(u)\ge k_0\) on \([ -\eta,\eta]^d\).  For every \(z\) the rescaled cube contains one of the finitely many orthant boxes of side \(\eta\wedge(1/2)\).  On such a box a nonzero polynomial \(v^\top b_r(u)\) cannot vanish almost everywhere.  Compactness of the unit sphere in the fixed-dimensional space \(\mathbb R^{q_r}\), followed by the density lower bound, therefore yields \(c_0>0\) such that
\[
c_0h^d\le\mathbb E_P[\ell_{z,h}(X_{st})\mid E_0],
\qquad
\mathbb E_P[v^\top\Phi_{z,h}(X_{st})v\mid E_0]
\ge c_0h^d\|v\|_2^2.
\tag{15}
\]
These bounds are uniform in \(s,t,z,h\).  Fix \(0<c_G<c_0/(4C_0)\).

Let \(A_0>2\lambda/d+2\) and set
\[
b_T=\lceil C_\beta\log(T\vee2)\rceil,
\]
where \(C_\beta\) is sufficiently large that
\[
T\beta_0\rho_0^{b_T}\le T^{-A_0}.
\tag{16}
\]
Partition \(\{1,\ldots,T\}\) into consecutive blocks of length at most \(b_T\), and divide them into odd and even subfamilies.  Consecutive blocks of a fixed parity are separated by at least \(b_T\) calendar indices.  From the definition of the conditional absolute-regularity coefficient, replacing one such block by an independent copy with the same marginal changes the probability of every event by at most \(\beta_P(b_T\mid E_0)\).  Replacing the blocks successively and telescoping total-variation distances therefore shows that either parity subfamily differs from the product of its block marginals by at most
\[
C(T/b_T)\beta_P(b_T\mid E_0)\le CT^{-A_0}.
\tag{17}
\]

Let \(F\) be either \(\ell_{z,h}\) or \(v^\top\Phi_{z,h}v\) with \(\|v\|_2=1\), and let \(W_g\) be the sum of \(F(X_{st})\) over block \(g\) in one parity.  Boundedness of \(K\) and of \(b_r\) on the support of \(K\) implies
\[
0\le W_g\le Cb_T,
\qquad W_g^2\le Cb_TW_g.
\]
Under the product law in (17), the \(W_g\)'s are independent, and (14)--(15) imply
\[
\sum_g\operatorname{Var}(W_g)
\le\sum_g\mathbb E[W_g^2]
\le Cb_TTh^d.
\tag{18}
\]
For \(V_g=W_g-\mathbb EW_g\), expansion of the exponential series and the bounds \(|V_g|\le Cb_T\) and \(\mathbb E[V_g^2]=\operatorname{Var}(W_g)\) give, whenever \(0<\theta<(Cb_T)^{-1}\),
\[
\mathbb E e^{\theta V_g}
\le\exp\left\{
\frac{\theta^2\operatorname{Var}(W_g)}{2(1-C\theta b_T)}
\right\}.
\tag{19}
\]
Multiplying (19), applying Chernoff's inequality, and optimizing \(\theta\) for a deviation of order \(Th^d\) gives
\[
P\left\{
\left|\sum_g(W_g-\mathbb EW_g)\right|>cTh^d
\right\}
\le C\exp\left(-c\frac{Th^d}{b_T}\right).
\tag{20}
\]
Apply (20) to both parity families and add the coupling error (17).

For the Gram matrix, apply the resulting scalar bound to \(v^\top\Phi_{z,h}v\) over a fixed \(1/4\)-net \(\mathcal V\) of the unit sphere.  Its cardinality is fixed because \(q_r\) is fixed.  For every symmetric matrix \(A\), approximation of a maximizing eigenvector by \(v\in\mathcal V\) gives
\[
\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\le2\max_{v\in\mathcal V}|v^\top Av|.
\tag{21}
\]
Equations (14)--(21) show that, outside an event of probability at most
\[
C\exp\left(-c\frac{Th^d}{b_T}\right)+CT^{-A_0},
\tag{22}
\]
the calendar-level mass is at most \(2C_0Th^d\), while the calendar-level Gram matrix is at least \((c_0/2)Th^dI_{q_r}\).  Replication multiplies both quantities by \(n_s\):
\[
L_s(h)=n_s\sum_{t=1}^{T}\ell_{z,h}(X_{st}),
\qquad
G_s(h)=n_s\sum_{t=1}^{T}\Phi_{z,h}(X_{st}).
\tag{23}
\]
Thus the candidate passes the normalized-shape test outside (22), and
\[
P\left\{L_s(h)=0\ \text{or}\
\lambda_{\min}\left(\frac{G_s(h)}{L_s(h)}\right)<c_G
\,\middle|\,E_0,\widetilde z_s\right\}
\le C\exp\left(-c\frac{Th^d}{b_T}\right)+CT^{-A_0}.
\tag{24}
\]
Notice that no response variable and no upper local-mass event occurs in (24).

Write \(h_0=h_{s,\beta}\).  If \(h_0<1\), its definition and a sufficiently large fixed \(C_h\) give
\[
\frac{T(2^vh_0)^d}{b_T}\ge c2^{vd}
\tag{25}
\]
for every dyadic candidate \(2^vh_0\le1\).  If selection has not stopped by that candidate, the candidate fails.  Substituting (25) in (24) proves
\[
P\{h_s>2^vh_{s,\beta}\mid E_0,\widetilde z_s\}
\le C\exp(-c2^{vd})+CT^{-A_0}.
\tag{26}
\]
When \(h_0=1\), the assertion is immediate.  At the terminal candidate \(h=1\), (24) gives
\[
P\{\text{terminal-grid failure}\mid E_0,\widetilde z_s\}
\le C\exp\{-cT/\log(T\vee2)\}+CT^{-A_0}.
\tag{27}
\]

Fix \(a>0\).  In (16) choose the auxiliary blocking constant large enough to replace \(A_0\) by any \(A_a>a/d+2\); this affects the proof blocks, not the estimator.  The dyadic tail sum and (26) yield
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E_P[h_s^a\mathbf1_{\mathrm{good}}\mid E_0,\widetilde z_s]
&\le h_0^a+
\sum_{v:\,2^vh_0<1}(2^{v+1}h_0)^a
P\{h_s>2^vh_0\mid E_0,\widetilde z_s\}\\
&\le Ch_0^a+CT^{-A_a}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{28}
\]
Here \(\sum_{v\ge0}2^{av}e^{-c2^{vd}}<\infty\), and the dyadic values are capped at one.  Expanding the definition of \(h_0\) proves the displayed moment bound.

There is only one selected fit per cohort.  A union bound over fixed \(S\) in (27) controls all selector failures.  Finite fourth donor moment makes \(\bar Z\) and its projection finite almost surely; a successful normalized Gram matrix is invertible; and \(M_4(N)\), \(q_N\), and \(\delta_N\) are finite for every positive \(N\).  Since fixed \(D\) and \(\alpha_{\mathrm{don}}>0\) imply \(q_N\le C\), one has \(\delta_N\le CN^{-1/2}\), so \(\delta_N\le\delta_0\) eventually.  For the finitely many smaller values, the deterministic bad-event indicator is at most \(CR_{\mathrm{don}}\).  Also, because \(A_0>2\lambda/d+2\),
\[
e^{-cT/\log(T\vee2)}+T^{-A_0}
\le C\left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}T\right\}^{2\lambda/d}
=CR_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}.
\tag{29}
\]
Consequently \(P(\mathrm{bad}\mid E_0)\le CR_{\star,\beta}\) along every stated array.  Finally,
\[
T\{(Tn_s)^{-1/(2\lambda+d)}\}^d
\quad\text{may be }O(1),
\qquad
Th_{s,\beta}^d\ge c\log(T\vee2).
\tag{30}
\]
The second relation, rather than a dense-site hypothesis, supplies (25).  This proves every assertion using geometric mixing of the design alone.
